title: Earth fault loop path
summary: Describes the earth fault loop path, its parts, and how earth loop impedance (Zs) is made up of the external impedance Ze and the consumer's R1 + R2.

sections.heading: Parts of the earth fault loop
paragraphs: The earth fault loop is the path fault current takes, starting at the point of the fault. Its total impedance is called the earth fault loop impedance, denoted Zs and measured in ohms (Ω).
bullets: Main earthing terminal (MET) and earthing conductor
For TN-S systems, the supply earth
The path through the earthed neutral point of the supply transformer
The line conductor from the source to the point of the fault

sections.heading: Ze and R1 + R2
paragraphs: The fault path splits into two parts. The external impedance (Ze) is the combined resistances and impedances of the fault path on the District Network Operator's (DNO) side of the supply intake.
The other part is the combined resistance of the consumer's line conductor (R1) and the consumer's cpc (R2), referred to as (R1 + R2). Both values combined form the earth loop impedance (Zs).
bullets: Ze: DNO side of the intake
R1 + R2: consumer's line conductor plus cpc

sections.heading: Earthing systems
paragraphs: The earth loop impedance is considered for TN-S, TN-C-S and TT systems. The deck shows each as a diagram, but the loop is always the fault path from the fault back to the source and through the source winding.
